title: Food Crisis is Coming...
description:
Most people think the Iran war will only affect oil and LPG prices. But the real crisis may be food. And the early signs are already visible.

India’s fertilizer ecosystem is already under pressure. Some urea plants are running at reduced capacity, gas allocations are being cut, and global fertilizer prices are rising rapidly. Behind the scenes, another key supply chain is also collapsing — sulphur, a critical input used in fertilizers, electronics, chemicals, and pharmaceuticals.

The problem is deeply interconnected. A large share of the world’s fertilizer trade passes through the Strait of Hormuz, the same chokepoint now under disruption. If this continues, fertilizer shortages could hit farmers, crop production could fall, and food prices could surge.

In this video, we break down what the fertilizer crisis really means, how it could impact India’s agriculture and economy, and why a geopolitical conflict thousands of kilometers away might soon show up in your grocery bill.
